title: Agriculture, Construction and Closed-Loop Habitats (partial interdisciplinary survey)
description: An eight-route, six-block partial survey joining agricultural site and resource boundaries, lighting and energy, water and control evidence, plant base-editing evidence, construction planning, closed-loop balances, a synthetic audit lab and an optional integrative project. It is unreviewed and formative-only, with no operational editing, construction or life-support instruction.

modifications: Original readings, synthetic datasets, worked examples, practice, retrieval cards and zero-point cases developed with substantial AI assistance on 2026-11-26. All third-party sources and owner repositories are link-only; no source content, code or data imported.

knowledge: Algebra, percentages, units and basic conservation balances
Foundational genetics, biochemistry and classical-mechanics concepts
prerequisites.statement: Genetics & Genomics, Biochemistry I and Physics: Mechanics are recommended prerequisites for their respective evidence and conceptual-load-path strands. This package establishes no university prerequisite equivalency.

outcomes.description: Define an agricultural system boundary, reconcile simple site inventories and identify claims that require local human review.
Calculate PPFD, DLI, photoperiod and lighting-energy quantities while distinguishing timer records and energy estimates from plant-response evidence.
Reconcile water and material inventories and evaluate climate-sensor and control evidence without creating nutrient recipes or autonomous operating instructions.
Appraise high-level plant base-editing evidence with controls, comparators, corrections and system-level limitations, without operational editing guidance.
Trace conceptual load paths and construct dependency-aware work plans with explicit engineering, permission and inspection gates, not real construction instructions.
Compute closed-loop energy, water and outage balances with explicit residuals and boundaries, without claiming life-support performance or habitability.
Audit a synthetic habitat CSV for arithmetic residuals, sensor gaps and control inconsistencies while preserving provenance and statistical independence boundaries.
Assemble an optional five-milestone integrative evidence package that joins site, light, water, biological-evidence, construction and outage boundaries.

lesson_objectives.description: Draw a system boundary that separates production zones, support flows, wastes and external dependencies.
Reconcile synthetic land, water and input inventories without mistaking accounting for impact proof.
Evaluate site evidence and identify permissions, safety and community questions reserved for local reviewers.
Convert between photosynthetic photon flux density and daily light integral with explicit time and unit conventions.
Compute lighting energy from fixture power and operating time, including independent checks of timer behaviour.
Interpret photoperiod, spatial light variation and energy records without inferring crop response from engineering quantities alone.
Close synthetic water and material-inventory balances with explicit initial stock, inputs, outputs and final stock.
Distinguish sensor readings, calibration evidence, missing data and spatial variation when interpreting climate records.
Evaluate feedback-control logs, actuator evidence and human fallback gates without treating a setpoint as a biological prescription.
Distinguish molecular editing outcomes from trait, agronomic and whole-system outcomes using appropriate comparators.
Interpret synthetic treatment and control counts while preserving independent-lineage, background-variant and assay limitations.
Use the Zong correction and Jin off-target study to evaluate evidence provenance, uncertainty and remaining review needs.
Trace a conceptual load from demand through structural members and supports to a foundation boundary without sizing real components.
Build a work breakdown and finish-to-start dependency network, calculating earliest completion from parallel and serial activities.
Place qualified design review, permits, inspection and change-control gates where a paper plan cannot authorize physical work.
Reconcile electrical supply and load energy over normal and backup intervals with explicit residual terms.
Reconcile stored water, new input, recovery and consumption without equating a recovery fraction with safety or autonomy.
Evaluate outage duration, critical-load assumptions and unmodelled hazards without making life-support or habitability claims.
Recompute every synthetic energy and water row and quantify any nonzero balance residual.
Identify missing sensors, timer conflicts and review-gate failures without converting absent data into zero values.
Report per-scenario findings without treating reused or correlated rows as independent replicates or as real habitat evidence.
Integrate site boundaries, lighting and resource balances into a traceable synthetic concept dossier.
Combine correction-aware biological evidence, conceptual load paths, dependencies and human decision gates without operational plans.
Rehearse outage and audit calculations and communicate assumptions, unresolved evidence and non-operational status in a final handoff.

duration.equivalent_structure: A proposed, unmeasured eight-block sequence of eight lesson routes grouped into six thematic blocks. The audit and optional project sit with closed-loop integration in block six; this is a partial survey, not a reviewed or complete university course.

lessons.title: Agricultural systems, inventories and site boundaries
lessons.worked_example: In an original synthetic site ledger, two production zones total 200 m² and 30 m² of shared paths are excluded, leaving 170 m² in the declared production boundary. Reclaimed water is 32% of the 100 L combined input. These arithmetic results describe the ledger only; they establish neither resource sustainability nor permission to develop the site.

lessons.title: PPFD, DLI, photoperiod, timers and lighting energy
lessons.worked_example: For an original synthetic array, PPFD 200 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ for 14 h gives DLI = 200 × 14 × 3600/10⁶ = 10.08 mol m⁻² d⁻¹. Four 0.12 kW fixtures over the same interval use 6.72 kWh. These values describe photons and electrical energy, not a plant-growth guarantee or an optimal lighting schedule.

modules.title: Water, nutrients, climate and control evidence

lessons.title: Water and nutrient inventories, climate sensors and control
lessons.worked_example: An original synthetic tank begins at 180 L, receives 40 L of new input and 30 L of recovered water, and records 70 L consumed; the closing inventory is 180 + 40 + 30 − 70 = 180 L. A separate material ledger ends at 5 mmol after transfers and estimated uptake. These are audit exercises, not nutrient dosing guidance or evidence of crop suitability.

modules.title: Plant base-editing evidence in system context

lessons.title: Plant base-editing evidence: controls, comparators and limitations
lessons.worked_example: In an original synthetic evidence table, 18 of 72 assessed plants show the declared molecular outcome, so 18/72 × 100 = 25%. A second table shows 14/60 treated and 6/60 comparator plants with a phenotype, a 13.33 percentage-point difference. Neither result identifies mechanism, excludes unintended variants or proves field performance.

modules.title: Construction systems, dependencies and human gates

lessons.title: Conceptual load paths, work breakdown and construction dependencies
lessons.worked_example: An original synthetic statics check splits a 12 kN conceptual vertical load equally between two idealized supports, giving 6 kN each; it says nothing about member adequacy. In a separate schedule, parallel 3-day and 4-day tasks precede a 2-day review, so earliest completion is max(3, 4) + 2 = 6 days.

lessons.title: Closed-loop habitat energy, water and outage balances
lessons.worked_example: An original synthetic outage supplies a 0.35 kW critical load for 8 h and therefore needs 2.8 kWh before any reserve or conversion-loss allowance. A separate water ledger closes at 150 + 12 − 30 = 132 L. These are transparent model balances, not evidence that a habitat can support people or survive an actual outage.

lessons.title: Synthetic-data habitat audit lab
lessons.worked_example: In the original synthetic audit CSV, row A03 records 30 kWh supplied and 28.8 kWh allocated, so the energy residual is +1.2 kWh. Its water residual is 138 + 30 + 40 − 50 − 156 = +2 L. The lab reports these per-row discrepancies and does not pool correlated scenarios into a confidence interval.

lessons.title: Optional integrative project guide: bounded habitat evidence package
lessons.worked_example: For original synthetic rehearsal row R02, DLI is 220 × 14 × 3600/10⁶ = 11.088 mol m⁻² d⁻¹. Row R03 closes at 90 + 20 + 28 − 46 = 92 L, and row R04 requires 0.30 × 6 = 1.8 kWh for its declared critical load. The project joins these checks with evidence and review gates, not a buildable habitat design.

grading_policy.attempt_policy: Unlimited formative retries; no summative grade is awarded.
grading_policy.solution_release: Public practice solutions may be shown after an attempt; case checklists are zero-point self-assessments.
grading_policy.late_policy: No deadlines or late penalties exist in this partial package.
grading_policy.appeals: No instructor review workflow is implemented; report ambiguous items as content issues.

accessibility.diagram_policy: No diagrams are included; boundaries, load paths and dependencies are expressed in prose and tables.
known_issues: Unicode units and equations require structured alternatives and assistive-technology review.
CSV tables have not undergone accessibility or usability review.

history.summary: New partial, unreviewed, formative-only interdisciplinary survey: eight routes in six blocks, eight original substantive readings, 48 public practice items worth 56 points, 24 retrieval cards, two original synthetic CSVs, one zero-point integrative case and five zero-point project milestones. All third-party sources and owner repositories are link-only. No operational plant editing, nutrient recipe, real construction or life-support instruction is supplied.

limitations: This eight-route, six-block package is a partial interdisciplinary survey, not a complete or measured university course. It is unreviewed and formative-only; no competency, credit, qualification or institutional authorization is established.

All scenarios, site values, plant counts, structural models, resource balances and CSV rows are original synthetic teaching data. Arithmetic closure is not physical validation, field performance, safety, habitability or life-support evidence.
Plant DNA editing is one evidence-literacy component only. The package supplies no guide/target design, delivery or regeneration procedure, sequence, operational parameter or laboratory protocol.

Water and material inventories teach conservation accounting only; no nutrient formulation, concentration target or dosing recipe is provided. Sensor and control examples do not authorize autonomous operation.

Construction content is limited to conceptual load paths, work breakdown, dependencies and human review gates. It supplies no site-specific engineering, member design, physical work instructions or inspection approval.
Habitat energy and water exercises are bounded spreadsheet models. They make no human-rating, life-support, environmental-safety, self-sufficiency or emergency-performance claim.
Synthetic audit rows may share scenario templates and are not independent replicates. Findings are reported per scenario without pooled reliability intervals or real-world causal inference.
Of the 24 numerical answers, 0 require units, 0 check significant figures and 0 check dimensions.

Third-party publications, official web materials and the four owner repositories are link-only. No third-party or owner-repository prose, figure, table, code, dataset or operational design is imported, and no endorsement or qualified review is implied.
intentionally_omitted: Guide/target design, editing delivery and regeneration steps, laboratory protocols and sequence-level exercises.
Nutrient formulations, dosing recipes and crop-specific operating prescriptions.
Real construction instructions, member sizing, site-specific structural calculations and physical-work authorization.
Human-rated habitat design, life-support certification, medical or emergency guidance and claims of safe occupancy.
Graded assessment, measured workload, qualified review, field trials and independently collected physical data.
